name: What is the difference between a feasibility assessment and a property appraisal?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a feasibility assessment and a property appraisal?

acceptedAnswer.text: A feasibility assessment focuses on the practical and regulatory viability of a construction project on a specific site, identifying potential challenges and opportunities before building. It considers factors like zoning, site conditions, and utility access to determine if a project can be built as envisioned. A property appraisal, conversely, determines the market value of an existing property or land. While both involve evaluating a site, their purposes differ significantly: feasibility looks forward to building, appraisal looks at current market worth.
acceptedAnswer.description: A feasibility assessment evaluates a project's buildability and viability, while a property appraisal determines the market value of land or an existing property.
